headline: Data Center Grid Cost Shifting
short_summary: This bill mandates that large energy users, primarily data centers, bear the costs of their increased electric generating capacity, preventing these costs from being passed to other ratepayers.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Residential ratepayers, consumer advocacy groups, potentially environmental groups.
opponents: Data center industry, large energy users.
news_headline: New Legislation Shifts Virginia Data Center Energy Costs to High-Demand Users
news_summary: Virginia lawmakers passed legislation requiring data centers and other large energy users (25 MW or more) to pay for increased generating capacity costs, preventing these expenses from being passed to other customers. This measure is part of a broader effort to regulate the state's growing data center industry.

headline: Data Center Water Use Reporting
short_summary: This bill requires water utilities to report monthly or quarterly on the volume of water supplied to data centers, increasing transparency on their water consumption.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Environmental groups, water conservation advocates, transparency advocates, local communities.
opponents: Data center industry (due to compliance burden), potentially those against increased regulation.
news_headline: As They Consider New Data Centers, States Target Water Use
news_summary: Virginia, along with other states, has enacted legislation like SB 553 to require water suppliers to report data center water consumption, aiming to provide transparency and help states understand projected and actual water demands from these facilities. This comes as lawmakers increasingly scrutinize data center resource use.

headline: Data Center Siting and Noise Limits
short_summary: This bill establishes a new permit process for high-energy-use data centers, requiring site assessments for noise impacts on nearby residences and schools, and allowing localities to assess other environmental and land-use effects.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local communities, residents near potential data center sites, environmental groups concerned about local impacts.
opponents: Data center developers (due to potential restrictions on site selection and increased development costs).
news_headline: Data Center Siting Restrictions Virginia Passed This Year
news_summary: Virginia passed new data center siting restrictions, including a permit process for facilities over 100 MW that requires sound assessments near homes and schools. Localities can also demand impact assessments on water, agriculture, and historic sites before approving projects, reflecting growing community concerns.
